newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gasoline hike won't hit inflation--Casas.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gasoline hike won't hit inflation--Casas.

text.p: A planned increase in Venezuelan gasoline prices will not have a major inflationary impact and does not alter the government's 30 to 35 percent 1997 inflation target, Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said.
"The 30 to 35 percent (inflation) target will be maintained. The increase in gasoline prices will not have a big effect," Casas told reporters during a forum on the financial sector.
Gasoline prices are due to increase by about 30 percent in the next few days, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Monday.
Venezuela's inflation rate in 1996 was 103.2 percent. So far this year, it has slowed dramatically to around 45 percent on an annual basis.
Economists say that salary increases and fiscal pressures make the government's target unlikely, and see inflation ending this year at around 45 to 50 percent.
